Developed by: BLACK HOLE STUDIO GOA Two Delhi Passengers Booked for Drinking Own Alcohol Aboard Delhi-Goa IndiGo Flight By Team Herald Published: 16 November 2026 Share SHARE Dabolim Airport Police have registered a non-cognisable offence against two Delhi residents for allegedly consuming alcohol brought by them aboard an IndiGo flight from Delhi to Goa. items.title: Shri Shantadurga Temple, Kavlem
items.hook: The goddess of peace, at Ponda in Goa.
paras: The Shri Shantadurga temple at Kavlem in Ponda is one of the most visited temples of the Gaud Saraswat community.
The name means the goddess of peace, and the temple's annual jatra is a major event in Goa.
items.wow: Several Goan temples, including this one, were moved inland in the 16th century to keep them safe.

items.title: Shri Mangesh Temple, Priol
items.hook: A Shiva temple closely tied to the community.
paras: The Shri Mangesh temple at Priol in Ponda is dedicated to Shiva and is closely tied to the Gaud Saraswat Brahmin community.
It is known for its deepstambha, its tank and its Goan architecture.
items.wow: The Mangesh temple's architecture mixes Goan and Konkani styles, and it is one of the best-known temples in Goa.

items.title: Konkani across four states
paras: Konkani is spoken along the western coast, from Maharashtra through Goa and coastal Karnataka to northern Kerala.
It is the official language of Goa and is written in Devanagari, though Roman script is widely used in Mangalore and Kochi.
items.wow: Konkani was added to the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution in 1992.

items.title: The Saraswat thread
items.hook: Chitrapur and Gaud Saraswat are not the same community.
paras: The Konkani Saraswat world has two large branches: the Gaud Saraswat Brahmins and the Chitrapur Saraswats.
The Gaud Saraswats follow the Partagali and Kashi maths; the Chitrapur Saraswats are centred on Shirali with their own math and traditions.
items.wow: Both share the Konkani language and a coastal heritage, but their maths and customs are distinct.

items.title: Kanhangad and Kochi
items.hook: Konkani families settled far down the coast.
paras: Konkani-speaking families settled in Kanhangad in northern Kerala and in Kochi over centuries, and their temples and community institutions are still active.
These communities keep the language alive well outside Goa and Karnataka.
items.wow: Konkani is spoken in four states today because of centuries of coastal trade and migration.
